newsitem.title: USA: TransTexas finds South Texas natgas field.
newsitem.headline: TransTexas finds South Texas natgas field.

text.p: TransTexas Gas Corp said Tuesday it is completing the 100 percent owned Laura Lopez No. 2 well as a discovery well for the Fandango South natural gas field in Jim Hogg County, midway between the company's Bob West North field and its Lobo Trend discoveries.
It said the find is located about seven miles southeast of the productive Fandango natural gas field.
Spokesman Simon Ward said the company hopes to begin production from the well before the end of the month.
TransTexas said it is constructing a 19-mile, 30-inch, 600 million cubic feet per day capacity pipeline lateral.

This will allow the transport of natural gas from Fandango south to the company's existing Thompsonville-to-Hebbronville 30-inch mainline and thus to the company's Agua Dulce marketing hub. This line will also carry gas from the company's Bob West North field to Agua Dulce.

Production can begin by month end if the pipeline is completed before deer hunting season begins in late November, Ward said, explaining the company's leases do not allow construction activity during deer season.

TransTexas said the Laura Lopez was drilled to a depth of 14,746 feet and will be completed in a 35 net feet pay zone of the Travis Ward sands in the Wilcox formation, within an interval between 13,596 and 13,640 feet.

The company said a similar well in the same horizon of an adjacent fault block is currently producing at 5 million cubic feet per day and has cumulative total production of over 17 billion cubic feet of natural gas.
"Given the higher porosity of 24 percent, as indicated by electric logs, and the pressure from this depth, it is anticipated that the payzone could prove to be highly productive," TransTexas said.
Citing the porosity, Ward said "this could be a very interesting well."

The company said a delineation well, the Laura Lopez No. 3, is drilling at a 12,400 feet and expected to reach projected depth in the targeted Fandango sands by mid-December. -- Jim Brumm 212-859-1710.
